transcript.text: Thank you all for flagging these items. Let me summarize what I'm hearing and how I see the path forward. Martin, your point about the non-recourse true sale at $11,400,000 is fundamental -- it means the draft proposal's reference to seller support for collection shortfalls has to be removed, and the purchase price needs to be adjusted to $11,400,000. Aisha, the $1,200,000 first-loss reserve for the concentration breach is a credit policy requirement, so that needs to be built into the structure. Jon, the lockbox activation commitment effective June 15, 2026 must be included as a closing condition. Nadia, the enhanced sanctions screening and its two-business-day documentation deadline must be added to the closing checklist. Before I authorize, I need to confirm one thing with the group: given that this is now a non-recourse true sale at $11.4 million, does anyone see an issue with the bank funding the $1.2 million first-loss reserve on its own balance as a condition to closing, rather than structuring it as seller recourse? Martin, I'm particularly interested in your view on whether a bank-funded reserve would be compatible with the true sale characterization.

transcript.text: Elena, that's an important question and I want to be careful with my answer. A bank-funded first-loss reserve held on our own balance is conceptually different from a seller guarantee of collection shortfalls -- the reserve is our own capital set aside, not a contractual promise to reimburse the buyer for shortfalls. That distinction generally supports true sale characterization because the buyer bears the collection risk and we are not contractually obligated to make up any deficit. However, I need to flag two things. First, the exact mechanics matter -- how the reserve is funded, whether it's released to the buyer or held separately, and whether the buyer has any claim to it beyond its stated purpose could all affect the analysis. Second, I have not yet seen Aisha's revised concentration worksheet or the specific credit policy language governing the first-loss reserve requirement, so I'd want to review those before giving definitive legal sign-off on the structure. My preliminary view is that a properly structured bank-funded reserve should be compatible with true sale, but I'd like to see the policy details and confirm the reserve mechanics with buyer's counsel before we finalize.
